title: PanelAlpha platform manifest
description: One deployable stack: how to recognise it, and the staged commands that build, install, upgrade and start it.

id.description: Unique manifest id; also the filename.

strategy.description: Strategy id the rest of the pipeline switches on. Defaults to `id`. Two manifests may share one strategy when a stack has two deployment shapes (astro / astro-ssr).

label.description: Human-readable name shown in deploy logs.

priority.description: Detection order, highest first. This is where ordering constraints live: Laravel must outrank PHP, Django must outrank Python, Next must outrank Vite.

app_root.description: The application's own root inside the repository, when they are not the same directory — phpBB ships its application in phpBB/ and keeps only build tooling at the top level. `detect` rules stay relative to the repository root (they run before this is known); everything after detection — the runtime version read from the project's manifests, the deployability check, the files copied into the image, and the document root — is resolved inside it. Must be a relative path that does not escape the repository.

docroot.description: Apache's document root, relative to the application root — `public` for Laravel and Flarum, `pub` for Magento, `upload` for OpenCart, `.` for an application served from its own root. Only meaningful for `runtime: php`, where the shared base image reads it as PA_DOCROOT. Omit it and the image looks for a `public/` directory and falls back to the application root, which is right for most PHP applications. Must be a relative path that does not escape the application.

build_args.description: Dockerfile ARG values the repository's own build needs in order to produce a deployable variant of itself — `BASE: apache` for a Dockerfile whose `FROM ${BASE}-base` picks between an FPM image and an Apache one. Only the `dockerfile` strategy reads it: `--target` stops the build at a stage, so it cannot select a variant the later stages of the file read.

system_packages.description: Debian packages to add to this application's PHP base image, for a binary the app execs that no PHP extension supplies — `ffmpeg` for a video site. Allowlisted (`PhpBaseImage::SYSTEM_PACKAGES`): each distinct set is a separate ~1.1 GB variant image the host builds once and only accounts deploying such an app load. The first deploy of a new set waits for that build, and fails rather than deploying without the packages. `runtime: php` only.

image.description: Literal base image. Omit and use `requires` when the version comes from the project.

requires.description: Toolchains this platform needs. Names only — never versions: a manifest describes every project of its kind, and the version is a property of one project. A Runtime class reads the project and answers. `role: build` means the toolchain builds the app and is absent from the runtime image, which is why a Laravel app that compiles assets needs no image containing both PHP and Node.

optional.description: Absent toolchain is not an error — a Laravel app with no package.json does not need Node.

output_from.description: Resolver for an output path the project declares itself (angular.json, vite.config, webpack.config) or that depends on a workspace.

commands_from.description: Command id => resolver, for commands whose text is derived from the project.

database.description: The platform needs a relational database and does not ship one. The engine provisions a database and user on the account's own MySQL server — visible in the panel, manageable in phpMyAdmin, and surviving a redeploy — and hands the app its credentials as DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_DATABASE, DB_USERNAME and DB_PASSWORD. Omit it for a platform whose project points itself at a database (Laravel reads its .env) or ships one in its own compose file.

check.description: Health checks this manifest adds to the ones its runtime already brings — `laravel/app-key-set`, not `php`. A whole group is `<group>`, one check is `<group>/<id>`. Never list your own runtime's group: `runtime: php` already brings `checks/php/`, and repeating it in fifteen manifests is the duplication the groups exist to remove. To skip a check a group brings, put a `when` guard on the check itself; a manifest whose application answers a shipped check wrongly by design lists it under `check_skip`.

check_skip.description: Shipped checks this application answers wrongly by design, each reported as skipped with its reason instead of run — Apaxy's product is the directory listing `_baseline/no-directory-listing` exists to fail. Name one check as `<group>/<id>`; it must be one this manifest is asked. A check of severity `error` can only be skipped with `covered_by` naming another `error` check this manifest is asked, which asks the question instead: a skip must not be able to hide an outage.

reason.description: Why the check does not apply. Shown in the health report.

covered_by.description: The check that asks the question instead. Required when the skipped check has severity error.

extra.description: Extra decision fields merged into the detection result.

runtime_image.description: Base image for the final stage when building and running want different images. {version} is substituted from the resolved runtime requirement. Requires output_directory: what the build stage produced is what gets copied in.

condition.description: Every key present must hold. An empty object matches nothing.

none.description: Negative rule: not one of these may match. This is how Static says 'an index.html and none of the manifests that would make this an application'.

path.description: File at a path relative to the project root.

probe.description: Named platform probe, for detection JSON cannot express. Discovered by class name under Platform/Probes.

id.description: Stable name shown in deploy logs. Derived from `run` when omitted.

stage.description: build = image build. install = first deploy only. upgrade = redeploy over existing data. start = every boot. A list means every listed stage — ['install','upgrade'] is how a migration says 'whenever the code changed, never on a restart'.

role.description: Build-stage only. `dependencies` runs before the source is copied so BuildKit can cache it across deploys that did not touch the lockfile.

serve.description: The long-running process. Exactly one per manifest, start stage only, exec'd as the final line of the entrypoint.

optional.description: A failure is logged and the boot continues.

before.description: Run this command ahead of the platform's own for the stage, rather than after.

when.description: Guard: the command applies only to projects matching this.

description.description: Why this command exists. Emitted as a comment in the entrypoint.
